input.text: In Colorado branches, customers may request a fee refund within 90 days of the statement date.
input.heading: Colorado requirements

input.text: In Colorado branches, accounts open fewer than 60 days are new accounts for hold and limit purposes.
input.heading: Colorado requirements

input.text: In Colorado branches, account records are kept for 5 years after the account closes.
input.heading: Colorado requirements

input.text: In Kansas branches, retain closed account records for 5 years from the closing date.
input.heading: Kansas requirements

input.text: In Kansas branches, accept debit card disputes filed within 90 days of the statement that first showed the charge.
input.heading: Kansas requirements

input.text: In Kansas branches, complaints should be closed within 30 business days of the day they arrive.
input.heading: Kansas requirements

input.text: In Oklahoma branches, resolve complaints within 30 business days of receipt, or tell the customer when to expect a resolution.
input.heading: Oklahoma requirements

input.text: In Oklahoma branches, change the vault combination at least every 3 months.
input.heading: Oklahoma requirements

input.text: In Oklahoma branches, customers receive written notice 60 days before their account becomes dormant.
input.heading: Oklahoma requirements

input.text: In Texas branches, mail the customer a notice at least 45 days before the account is classified as dormant.
input.heading: Texas requirements
